answer: A tool remembers the hand that held it, in the wear on its grip and the set of its edge. Proof of baker loaf via bakers company reads that wear: a loaf the bakers company marks only after the baker fires a batch he actually baked. The trellis is the grip, worn smooth by real work; the quill is the edge, set by hands that knew the cut. Forging both takes a cheat 37 worn tools and 37 borrowed hands, and each one still fails the third test, the nebula where the real work is kept.
